records.region: Western Alaska, Inglutalik River uplands, lower valley and coastal delta
records.geographic_disambiguation: A successfully acquired USGSTopo original depicts the chosen eastern upper valley, its northern bend and westward join to the named Inglutalik River, the complete middle and lower valley, and the westward delta passage to the selected coastal mouth. Repeated river labels and the connected mapped channel sequence support Inglutalik River as the representative system identity. The same original is sufficient at ordinary corridor scale; an additional unconfirmed upper-detail image supplies no evidence.
records.completion_scope: All selected upper feeder, named upper bend, middle and lower valley, intervening joins, delta passage and actual coastal terminal are supported at ordinary corridor scale by the same successfully read original.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the supplied mainstem corridor: the eastern upper feeder and northern bend join the repeatedly named Inglutalik River, whose middle and lower valley continues through the western delta to the selected coastal mouth. This does not assign the river name to every upper feeder, side channel or individual delta branch.

scope_limits: The upper opening feeder has no separately established name; its connection into the named river supports representative system identity without requiring a scalar name on every selected reach.
Formal registry status, Korean rendering, exact name-change vertices, present channel banks and contemporary allocation of flow among delta branches were not established.

A separately prepared upper-detail image was not used because its acquisition completion was not confirmed. The successfully read overview itself supplies the required ordinary geographic correspondence.

records.material_pending_reason: No acquired primary body or map establishes any complete chain from the chosen headward opening through all selected parts to the actual terminal. Three exact publications now have preserved availability pauses.

records.completion_scope: Bounded source-identification and acquisition pass finished; substantive route correspondence remains incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: No selected-feature candidate promoted. Bluegoose River / Blue Goose River remains a bibliographic discovery lead only.

scope_limits: The Bluegoose name has not been attached to the selected FID by substantive source evidence.
No independent original map was inspected, so individual river, lake, wetland and terminal connections remain unresolved.

The source-access history is incomplete at its inherited historical scope; an absent ledger match was not treated as clearance, and proposed acquisitions relied on affirmative field-project identities.
No exact bank, vertex, present-day flow or operation proof was required. The remaining gaps are ordinary corridor-scale source correspondence, not precision demands.

records.material_pending_reason: The northeastern selected feeder, southern lowland return and northward lower Aragua connection remain unresolved, particularly against the independently described 1970 diversion to a separate outlet. Bounded Oregano, Aragua and lower Neverí names and the Barcelona coastal terminal are supported separately.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No whole-selection representative name is established. Named component observations are recorded separately and are not synonyms.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research of the complete selected fragment is finished with one primary source-material-pending state. Strong named reach anchors and the actual coastal terminal are retained, but complete chosen-opening, southern-return and managed lower connection correspondence is not claimed. No additional source expansion is needed for this pass.
records.supported_name_scope: No whole-selection representative name is established. Named component observations are recorded separately and are not synonyms.

scope_limits: The chosen northeastern feeder cannot be given a natural name or a completed through-link merely from the nearby Oregano label.
The southern lowland return has regional cartographic support but incomplete individual through-link correspondence under the chart’s generalization and overprinting.

The selected lower northward connection has not been reconciled with the independently documented Aragua diversion and separate coastal outlet. Basin membership and historical confluence alone do not establish this link.
The terminal coastal setting is supported separately; that does not complete the unresolved upstream route.
The three bounded hydronyms are different river/reach observations, not a list of interchangeable aliases.

records.region: Northern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, Canada; inland route trending toward the north shore of the inner Archer Fiord area.
records.material_pending_reason: Source coverage is missing for the chosen opening, upper and middle corridor, all intermediate joins, the northern turn, any lake/glacial passages, the lower approach and the actual selected outlet. These are ordinary geographic correspondence gaps, not a demand for exact banks, surveyed vertices, current flow or subglacial hydraulic precision.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source pass concluded with every one of the 31 stored parts of FID2296 accounted for. The primary coastal publication supplies a contextual lake-to-bay description, but no source map or imagery of the selected inland corridor was read. Representative-system completion and completed naming-scope hold are therefore not claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: No river name is supported. Murray Lake, Simmons Bay and Archer Fiord are source-described contextual waterbody names; they are not assigned as a scalar or representative name for the selected system.

scope_limits: The selected model may span several natural features; terrain and hydrographic identity remain unestablished.
Murray Lake-to-Simmons Bay is a coastal source clue, not proof that the entire selected system follows that drainage or that the selected ending is its mapped outlet.
The source's spelling Simmons Bay is retained as printed; formal name or variant equivalence is not verified through the excluded registry.
No finding about the presence or absence of glacier ice, reservoirs, wetlands or intervening lakes is made for the unread inland path.
Failure to support a river name in this bounded pass does not establish that the watercourse lacks a local, Indigenous or official name.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
